chunks: From him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl, from Abān ibn Taghlib, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام.

Concerning a man who performed one circuit or two circuits, then went out with another man regarding his need, he said: If it was a supererogatory tawaf, he builds upon it; and if it was an obligatory tawaf, he does not build upon it.

key_terms.حَاجَتِهِ: his need or matter requiring assistance
key_terms.طَافَ: performed tawaf, i.e. circumambulated the Kaʿbah
key_terms.لَمْ يَبْنِ عَلَيْهِ: he does not continue from where he left off
key_terms.يَبْنِي عَلَيْهِ: he continues from where he left off

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on interrupting obligatory or supererogatory tawaf before completing seven circuits?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about interrupting tawaf before completing seven circuits. If the interrupted tawaf was supererogatory, one may resume from where he left off, but if it was obligatory, he does not resume on that basis.
